prompt: I ran a paid manual pilot for a fictional invoice-chasing assistant. Six unrelated freelancers paid, four used it again, and I measured 35 minutes of delivery work per customer. Should I automate it now?
expected_behaviors: Classify inspected payments and measured delivery time as verified only if the artifacts were actually provided; otherwise classify them as user statements.
Separate repeat-use evidence from proof of scalable acquisition.
Approve only the next bounded automation stage, not an unrestricted build.
Define pass and stop lines plus time and money caps for the next stage.

prompt: I already spent eight weekends building a meal-planning prototype. Five friends love it and say I should launch. I am exhausted but want a 90/100 score tonight so I can commit the next three months.
expected_behaviors: Refuse to invent a numeric score without a complete user-supplied rubric and evidence.
Classify friend praise as an early signal rather than payment evidence.
Treat the prototype and time spent as test assets or sunk cost, not justification for more investment.
Propose a small test with unrelated target payers and a stop line.

prompt: A fictional industry report says the AI study market is growing quickly. My three posts received 2,000 likes, but I have no offer, buyer interviews, or payment attempts. Is that enough to build a subscription app?
expected_behaviors: Keep the market report as external inference rather than project-level demand.
Treat likes as a distribution signal, not buyer fit or payment evidence.
Mark buyer, payment, delivery economics, and retention as unknown.
Test a costly commitment before recommending a subscription build.

prompt: I have one paragraph describing a side-project idea and no customer evidence. Do not ask questions; tell me what to do next.
expected_behaviors: Give a conditional decision without blocking on questions.
Mark missing evidence as unknown rather than zero.
Provide no more than three next actions and include explicit caps.
